prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Conservative Party Manifesto 2019 – Summary (≤500 words)

Core message
- “Get Brexit done” with Boris Johnson’s deal: leave the EU in January 2020, no extension beyond Dec 2020, outside the single market/customs union and ECJ; legislate to maintain high standards; pursue global free trade deals while keeping close, friendly EU cooperation.

Economy and tax
- Invest while keeping debt under control; public investment capped at 3% of GDP. No rises in the rates of income tax, VAT or National Insurance. Raise NI threshold to £9,500 next year; ambition for first £12,500 tax-free. Raise National Living Wage to two-thirds of median pay by 2024. Maintain pension triple lock and key pensioner benefits.

NHS and social care
- Record funding settlement; 40 new hospitals/20 upgrades; 50,000 more nurses; 6,000 more GPs and 50m extra GP appointments; NHS Visa to recruit staff. Mental health treated with same urgency as physical health; Innovative Medicines Fund; clamp down on health tourism; hospital parking free for those in greatest need; NHS not on the table in trade talks.
- Social care: £1bn extra each year; cross-party plan with guarantee no one must sell their home to pay for care; one week’s unpaid carers leave; double dementia research funding.

Education and skills
- £14bn more for schools; minimum per-pupil funding; teacher starting salaries to £30k; uphold discipline/Ofsted; “arts premium,” PE investment; major SEN funding.
- £3bn National Skills Fund; expand apprenticeships, Institutes of Technology; upgrade FE colleges.

Crime and justice
- 20,000 more police; fair, proportionate stop and search; tougher sentences for serious crimes; more prison places; parole and criminal justice reviews; new national cyber crime force; Victims’ Law; Domestic Abuse Bill.

Immigration
- Australian-style points-based system; fewer low-skilled migrants; equal treatment of EU/non-EU; 5-year wait for most benefits; higher NHS surcharge; fast tracks for NHS staff and top global talent; fix Windrush injustices.

Infrastructure, towns and devolution
- “Infrastructure revolution”: Northern Powerhouse Rail (Leeds–Manchester first), Midlands Rail Hub, EV charging network, bus and cycling upgrades, restore select Beeching lines, contactless ticketing; HS2 under review; gigabit broadband nationwide by 2025.
- Towns Fund, cultural and community ownership funds; English Devolution White Paper; protect local democracy on council tax rises.

Housing
- Target 300,000 homes a year; support long-term fixed-rate mortgages and local/key worker discounts; maintain Right to Buy; reform leasehold.
- Renters’ reforms: end “no-fault” evictions; single “lifetime” deposit. Renew Affordable Homes Programme; end rough sleeping by end of Parliament. Infrastructure-first planning, local design codes, stronger building safety, greener homes, protect/enhance Green Belt.

Business, innovation and work
- Cut and review business rates; clamp down on late payments; boost start-up loans; review Entrepreneurs’ Relief; raise R&D tax credit to 13%; reduce red tape; support self-employed.
- Raise R&D to 2.4% of GDP; new high-risk research agency; strengthen life sciences; invest in data/computing; 2022 Festival of Great Britain and NI.
- Single enforcement body for workers’ rights; right to request predictable contracts; flexible working by default (consultation); more childcare; neonatal leave; a week of unpaid carers leave.

Rural, coastal, farming and fishing
- Replace CAP with “public money for public goods”; “Buy British” in public sector; expand seasonal workers; leave CFP, manage waters as an independent coastal state; tackle rural crime; improve rural transport.

Environment and climate
- Net Zero by 2050; Environment Bill and new watchdog; £640m Nature for Climate fund, trees/peatland restoration; plastics crackdown and deposit return scheme; fracking moratorium.
- 40GW offshore wind by 2030; carbon capture cluster by mid-2020s; £9.2bn for energy efficiency; clean air laws; consult on earliest petrol/diesel phase-out.

Union, democracy, defence and foreign policy
- Strengthen the Union; oppose a second Scottish independence referendum; Shared Prosperity Fund; freeports across UK; protect NI’s internal UK market access.
- Constitutional changes: repeal Fixed-term Parliaments Act; voter ID; fair boundaries; review HRA/judicial review; repeal Section 40; no Leveson 2.
- Defence: spend >2% GDP and grow in real terms; maintain Trident; Space Command; support veterans (NI cuts for employers, railcard, childcare, legal protections).
- Global values: Magnitsky sanctions; 0.7% aid; girls’ education; media freedom; LGBT conference; lead on climate (COP26); ambitious trade deals (US, AUS, NZ, Japan), services trade push; NHS and standards not up for negotiation.

Animal welfare
- Tougher cruelty sentences; crack down on puppy smuggling; animal sentience law; end long live-transport; extend ivory ban; ban primates as pets; stronger measures against cat theft.
